name: PrimitiveName
comment: The floating primitive; None uses the actor's root.

name: HullModel
comment: How the body meets the water: the hull surface (boats), voxels (logs, crates) or spheres (pontoons: balls, small props).

name: HullResolutionCm
comment: The hull is rebuilt from the simple collision as an even shell of triangles about this size, so the water line is followed across big faces (coarser if Max Hull Triangles is reached).

name: MaxHullTriangles
comment: The most triangles the hull may have; past it the shell is made coarser than Hull Resolution. More follows the water line more closely and costs more every physics step. The farther levels of detail get a quarter and a sixteenth of it.

name: LodDistancesCm
comment: Distances from the camera. Triangles model: beyond the first the hull is twice as coarse, beyond the second four times. Every model: beyond the first a slam throws only its main splash (no crown and no plunge splashes) and only while the frame's splash budget is less than half spent (fnb.Effects.SplashBudgetPerFrame); beyond the second, or when the body has not been drawn for a second, no splashes or spray at all.

name: VoxelSizeCm
comment: Voxels model: cube size (0: about Voxel Count of them fill the hull).

name: VoxelCount
comment: Voxels model: about how many cubes fill the hull when Voxel Size is 0. More follows the shape more closely and costs more.

name: Pontoons
comment: Spheres model: the pontoons (body frame). Empty: two rows along the hull's bottom, lifting what the whole hull would.

name: bSleepWhenSettled
comment: Once settled (barely moving for two seconds), out of sight and farther than Sleep Distance from the camera, the body sleeps and the water leaves it alone until it is seen, comes near, or something hits it.

name: SleepDistanceCm
comment: A settled body sleeps only when at least this far from the camera (and out of sight); it wakes when it comes nearer.

name: MassMode
comment: Where the body's mass comes from: Rest Draft sets it at Begin Play to what the hull displaces at Rest Draft; Body Mass keeps its own (Physics → Mass), and it floats wherever that puts it, or sinks.

name: RestDraftCm
comment: How deep the hull's lowest point sits in calm water, at rest.

name: bSettleOnStart
comment: Held still at Begin Play until its water has been read, then set level at its rest draft on that water and released: no drop or slam at the start.

name: RestAttitude
comment: How the body floats relative to its own frame: zero for a mesh modelled the way up it floats (a boat); a log or barrel modelled standing up floats lying down with Pitch 90. Rest Draft, the stability check and Settle On Start use it.

name: MaxDepenetrationSpeed
comment: How fast physics may push the body out of something it starts in or is pressed into (rocks under the water): low, so a bad placement eases out instead of launching it. 0 leaves the project setting.

name: CenterOfMassOffset
comment: Moves the centre of mass (body frame): lower is more stable. The hull analysis reports the metacentric height.

name: InertiaScale
comment: Scales the body's inertia (a hollow hull turns more slowly than a solid one of the same shape).

name: BuoyancyMultiplier
comment: Art control on the lift. 1 is Archimedes.

name: PressureDragLinear
comment: Pressure drag where a face pushes into the water: the part that grows with its speed through the water (speed / 1 m/s; Kerner's Cpd1).

name: PressureDragQuadratic
comment: Pressure drag where a face pushes into the water: the part that grows with the square of its speed through the water ((speed / 1 m/s)²; Kerner's Cpd2).

name: PressureFalloff
comment: How the pressure drag falls off as a face turns from meeting the flow head-on: it is scaled by cos^Falloff of the angle between the face's normal and the flow (Kerner's fp). Lower keeps more drag on slanted faces.

name: SuctionDragLinear
comment: Suction where a face pulls away from the water (behind the hull): the part that grows with its speed through the water (speed / 1 m/s; Kerner's Csd1).

name: SuctionDragQuadratic
comment: Suction where a face pulls away from the water: the part that grows with the square of its speed through the water ((speed / 1 m/s)²; Kerner's Csd2).

name: SuctionFalloff
comment: How the suction falls off as a face turns from facing straight away from the flow: it is scaled by cos^Falloff of that angle (Kerner's fs). Lower keeps more suction on slanted faces.

name: ViscousMultiplier
comment: Skin friction (ITTC 1957 line).

name: SlamMultiplier
comment: Slamming when faces drive into the water (bow slap, landing from a drop).

name: FlowCoupling
comment: How much the current carries the body (0 ignores it, 1 is physical).

name: AirDragCoefficient
comment: Drag on the dry part from the air and the wind.

name: AngularDamping
comment: Extra damping about the body's roll, pitch and yaw axes while wet (1/s). Zero leaves it to the water.

name: bPropulsion
comment: A propeller and rudder (body frame). Throttle and Rudder are set from Blueprint, or the console for testing (fnb.Boat.Throttle, fnb.Boat.Rudder) when Console Control is on.

name: bConsoleControl
comment: For testing: a change of fnb.Boat.Throttle or fnb.Boat.Rudder sets this body's Throttle and Rudder. Off: only Blueprint sets them.

name: ThrustLocation
comment: Where the propeller pushes, in the body's frame. It pushes only while it is under the water.

name: ThrustDirection
comment: Which way the propeller pushes at full ahead, in the body's frame (zero: forward, +X); astern pushes the other way.

name: MaxThrustNewtons
comment: The propeller's push at full throttle, newtons.

name: PropWashSpeed
comment: The propeller's wash over the rudder at full throttle, so the boat steers when slow.

name: RudderLocation
comment: Where the rudder sits, in the body's frame. It steers only while it is under the water.

name: RudderAreaCm2
comment: The rudder blade's area, cm²: its side force grows with it and with the square of the water's speed past the rudder (the boat's speed through the water plus the propeller's wash). 0: no rudder.

name: MaxRudderAngle
comment: The rudder's angle at Rudder -1 or 1.

name: Throttle
comment: -1 (full astern) to 1 (full ahead).

name: Rudder
comment: -1 (hard left) to 1 (hard right).

name: bWake
comment: Pushes the water: the pieces of water line driving into it (sideways, or outward as the hull sinks in: a drop makes a ring) are written into FluidNinja's data channel as moving brush points, so the simulation makes the bow wave, the wake and foam (Project Settings → FluidNinja Buoyancy → Wake; console fnb.Buoyancy.Wake). This works without tags or overlap events. It is separate from FluidNinja's own tracking (Generate Overlap Events on the floating primitive), which paints the body's pivot point; the two can run together.

name: Interaction
comment: How the body stirs the simulation: FluidNinja's own tracking relative to the water (the default, which needs the modified FluidNinja: Project Settings → FluidNinja Buoyancy → FluidNinja Tracking; console fnb.Buoyancy.Tracking), or the plugin's wakes. FluidNinja's tracking as it is today paints a body's world velocity, and a floater carried by a current then speeds that current up, so a body is handed to it only when every NinjaLive says it tracks relative to the water and paints no density for tracked bodies (Tracked Density Switch 1, 4 or 5).

name: WakeBrushSizeCm
comment: Brush size of each wake point at a push of 2 m/s (scaled 0.4–2x with the push).

name: WakeMinPushCmS
comment: Pieces of water line pushing into the water slower than this leave no wake.

name: WakeGain
comment: Each frame a wake point gives the water this share of what it lacks: the hull's outward speed there minus the water's own. FluidNinja adds brush velocity every frame, so the water near the hull approaches the hull's speed and never overshoots it. A body that makes wakes, or that FluidNinja tracks itself (Generate Overlap Events on), takes its current from the water around it, not from the water it has just pushed.

name: WakeStrength
comment: How much of the hull's speed through the water (relative to the current around it) the water at the hull takes on. A hull stirs only the water near the surface, not the whole depth FluidNinja's flat simulation stands for: 1 would make it a wall through the water (the current then races round it), 0 leaves the water alone. A body drifting with the current makes none.

name: PlungeGain
comment: The impact burst: where the hull sinks into the water (a drop, a dunk, a flat bottom slapping down), the water it displaces runs outward across the water line at about the sinking speed. This scales that outward speed: 1 is physical, 0 leaves only the side wake. A radial burst carries no net momentum, so it cannot build a current.

name: PlungeResponse
comment: Each frame a burst point gives the water this share of what it lacks of the burst's outward speed (as Wake Gain does for the side wake): higher makes the ring start faster and harder.

name: bWaves
comment: The body takes part in FluidNinja Waves (Project Settings → FluidNinja Buoyancy → Waves): its static head (how deep its hull sits below the wave-free surface) and the impulse of the slam and drag that stop it make real water waves in FluidNinja's simulation, which spread, bounce off banks and rock other floaters; and it feels the others' waves (its own taken out, its own waves' drag put back as radiation damping). Off: it floats on FluidNinja's own surface and leaves the waves alone.

name: WaveFeelScale
comment: Scales how much of the waves this body feels (κ, with Project Settings → FluidNinja Buoyancy → Waves → Wave Feel Scale): 1 is physical, 0 floats it on FluidNinja's own surface while it still makes waves.

name: bWetLine
comment: Darkens and glosses the hull below the water line and where it was wet a moment ago, drying at Drying Speed. The hull's materials read it as Custom Primitive Data (Wet Line Data Index … +3: the water line plane in the mesh's local space, and how far above it the hull is still wet). Add the material function MF_FNB_HullWetness to the hull's material to show it.

name: DryingSpeedCmS
comment: How fast the wet band above the water line dries, from the top down (and the whole hull once it is out of the water).

name: WetLineDataIndex
comment: The first of the four Custom Primitive Data slots the wet line writes on the floating primitive (this index … +3); move it when the hull's materials use those slots for something else.

name: SplashSystem
comment: Spray where the hull slams into the water and at the bow when it drives hard into it. None: the project default (FluidNinja Buoyancy → Effects).

name: SplashMinWatts
comment: Slams at least this strong (watts) throw a splash where they hit (the noise floor: a bobbing body's small slams make none). Its size is on the project's splash scale (FluidNinja Buoyancy → Effects → Splash Reference Watts), the same for every body. The body's entry (going in after being clear of the water) does not use this floor: it splashes whenever its own entry power makes a splash of at least 0.2 on that scale. 0: no slam splashes (entries and bow spray still run).

name: MaxSplashStrength
comment: The largest a splash from this body gets: its size is the cube root of the slam's (or entry's, or bow spray's) power over Splash Reference Watts (eight times the power, twice the splash), up to this many times the splash system's own size (before Splash Scale) and never past the project's Splash Strength Ceiling. Splashes under 0.2 are not drawn. Up to three more splashes go where the water line plunges in hardest, smaller by how much slower it plunges there.

name: BowSprayMinPushCmS
comment: When nothing slams, spray is thrown where the water line drives into the water at least this fast (the bow), on the project's splash scale: the power of the water that piece of water line drives in (its area × the cube of its speed), so twice the speed is twice the spray. 0: no bow spray.

name: SplashScale
comment: Scales the size of every splash and spray from this body.

name: SplashInterval
comment: The least time between two slam splashes from this body, and between two bow sprays. A slam does not wait for the bow spray's interval (it cuts in), and a slam that could not splash yet keeps its hardest value for a quarter of a second, so one-frame slams on a spraying bow are not lost.

name: SlapSound
comment: A one-shot played where the hull slams into the water (Slap Min Watts), louder the harder the slam. Float inputs a MetaSound can read are set on it: "Pitch Shift" (semitones), "Impact" (the slam on the project's splash scale, Splash Reference Watts), "Speed" (the water running past the water line, cm/s), "Length" (the water line, cm) and "Mass" (the body, kg). None: the project default (Project Settings → FluidNinja Buoyancy → Effects; no sounds ship with the plugin).

name: WashSound
comment: A loop played while the hull is in the water: the water running along the hull, louder and higher the faster it runs past the water line (Wash Full Speed) and the longer the water line; quiet lapping at rest. Its "Pitch Shift" input (semitones) follows the speed; "Impact", "Speed", "Length" and "Mass" are kept up to date on it as on the slap. None: the project default (Project Settings → FluidNinja Buoyancy → Effects; no sounds ship with the plugin).

name: CreakSound
comment: A one-shot played when the hull is thrown about (Creak Min Angular Acceleration) or slams four times Slap Min Watts; "Pitch Shift" (semitones), "Impact", "Speed", "Length" and "Mass" are set on it as on the slap. None: the project default (Project Settings → FluidNinja Buoyancy → Effects; no sounds ship with the plugin).

name: DripSound
comment: A one-shot played once when the hull leaves the water entirely: water dripping off it. Its float input "Impact" is set to how high the hull is wet above its last water line (cm), so a MetaSound can drip longer from a hull that went in deeper. None: no drip (there is no project default).

name: Attenuation
comment: How the hull's sounds fade with distance. None: the project default (Project Settings → FluidNinja Buoyancy → Effects).

name: SoundVolume
comment: Scales the volume of all of this body's hull sounds.

name: SlapMinWatts
comment: Slams at least this strong (watts) play a slap; four times this also creaks. 0: no slaps, and no creaks from slams.

name: WashFullSpeedCmS
comment: The wash is at full volume when the water runs past the water line this fast.

name: CreakMinAngularAcceleration
comment: Creaks when the hull's spin changes faster than this (rad/s²), or on a hard slam.

name: SlamEventWatts
comment: Slams weaker than this (watts) raise no event.

name: bEnabled
comment: Floating bodies feel the water. Console: fnb.Buoyancy -1 this setting (the default), 0 off, 1 on, 2 on with the debug view.

name: SurfaceTags
comment: Actors carrying one of these tags draw the water surface: FluidNinja's river spline pieces (SplineSource), its sea surfaces (SeaSurface), and any surface you tag FluidNinjaBuoyancySurface (a pool plane, a Niagara water sheet). The height capture shows only their surface primitives, leaving out a waterfall's face (steeper than 45 degrees).

name: NinjaParameterCollection
comment: FluidNinja's material parameter collection: where a simulation that follows the player is (TraceMeshPos, TraceMeshSize in metres). Simulations that set those parameters on their surface material instead are found from the material.

name: VelocityBufferParameter
comment: The surface material's texture parameter holding the simulation's velocity (RG) and density (B).

name: CaptureWidthCm
comment: Width of the square the drawn water is captured over, centred on the simulation that follows the player, else on the first floating body (FluidNinja's river template: 80 m).

name: CaptureResolution
comment: Texels across the capture (1024 over 80 m: 7.8 cm).

name: NearPlaneAboveBodiesCm
comment: The capture looks down from this far above the highest floating body (or the water under it): water higher up, such as a river passing over a pool, is above its near plane and left out.

name: FootprintMarginCm
comment: The water read back around each body: its bounds plus this, plus how far it moves in FootprintLeadSeconds.

name: bGPUGather
comment: Many bodies: one compute pass resamples every body's water (height and current) onto its own grid and one readback brings it all back, instead of two copies and two readbacks per body. Console: fnb.Buoyancy.Gather -1 this setting (the default), 0 the per-body copies, 1 the gather (A/B).

name: MaxGatherGrid
comment: A body's grid points are one capture texel apart, two beyond its first hull level-of-detail distance and four beyond the second; at most this many across (a larger body is sampled more coarsely).

name: MaxGatherBodies
comment: Bodies gathered in one frame at most; with more, they take turns.

name: MaxExtrapolationSeconds
comment: The read-back water is a few frames old: its heights are carried forward by their rate of change for at most this long.

name: FlowScaleMultiplier
comment: The current (cm/s) is the velocity buffer × SimSpeed × cell size × simulation steps per second × this. The steps per second are the fixed tick of FluidNinja's NinjaLiveCore system (1/60 s: 60 steps a second at any frame rate); a NinjaLiveCore without a fixed tick steps at FluidNinja's SamplingFPS, at most the frame rate.

name: MaxFlowSpeedCmS
comment: Currents faster than this are clamped (the buffer is clamped at FluidNinja's VelocityClamp).

name: WaterDensity
comment: Water density (kg/m³).

name: AirDensity
comment: Air density (kg/m³) for the dry part of a hull.

name: bStableSteps
comment: Keeps light bodies (balls, small props) stable whatever the physics step: the part of the water's spring (lift) and drag that a step is too long for is applied implicitly, as if the step had been cut finer. Bodies the step resolves well are untouched, so it works with the engine's default physics (one step a frame, any frame rate), substepping or async physics. Console: fnb.Buoyancy.Implicit -1 this setting (the default), 0 plain explicit forces, 1 stable steps (A/B).

name: Wind
comment: The wind on the dry part of hulls (cm/s, world).

name: bWakes
comment: Bodies push the water: each frame, the pieces of water line driving into it are written to FluidNinja's point input (its global Niagara Data Channel: Position, PositionPrevious, VelocityAndSize), so the simulation makes their bow waves, wakes and foam, which rock everything else. The FluidNinja simulation must read that channel (its DataChannelPointReaderEnabled on). The project default: each body's Wake switch can turn its own off, and its Interaction chooses wakes, FluidNinja's tracking or both. Console: fnb.Buoyancy.Wake -1 this setting (the default), 0 no wakes at all (the swimmers' too), 1 on (A/B).

name: MaxWakePoints
comment: At most this many wake points a frame for all bodies (FluidNinja reads up to its DataChannelThroughput, 4000).

name: TrackingTagProperty
comment: FluidNinja's own tracking, for bodies whose Interaction asks for it: the NinjaLive property (on the actor or its NinjaLive component) holding the component tag it tracks, FluidNinja's Track Actor Primitive Components With Tag. A body handed to the tracking gets that tag, besides Generate Overlap Events, which FluidNinja's tracking needs either way.

name: ObjectTypeFilterProperty
comment: The NinjaLive property (on the actor, or failing that its NinjaLive component) listing the object types it tracks, FluidNinja's Overlap Filter Inclusive Obj Type. A body is handed to the tracking only if a NinjaLive whose interaction volume overlaps it will select it: its object type is in that NinjaLive's list, or that NinjaLive tracks by tag (the plugin adds the tag). Otherwise the log says why it is not tracked.

name: InteractionVolumeComponent
comment: The NinjaLive component whose bounds are where it tracks (FluidNinja's InteractionVolume). A body outside every NinjaLive's volume is not handed over until it enters one; a NinjaLive without this component selects nothing.

name: RelativeTrackingSwitch
comment: How a NinjaLive says its tracking paints a body's velocity relative to the water under it (instead of its world velocity, which makes a current speed itself up around floating bodies): a bool or number property of this name on the NinjaLive actor or one of its components, or a float user parameter of its simulation; on above 0.5. FluidNinja does not have this yet; the name is the proposal (see the user guide, "FluidNinja's own tracking"). Bodies are handed to the tracking only while every NinjaLive in the level says so, and also paints no density for them (Tracked Density Switch). Console: fnb.Buoyancy.Tracking.

name: TrackedDensitySwitch
comment: How a NinjaLive says tracked bodies paint velocity but no density: FluidNinja's Selectively Kill Brush Density Keep Velocity, a number property of this name on the NinjaLive actor or one of its components, or an int user parameter of its simulation (User.Painter.<name> or User.<name>). 1 (ARRAY: primitives and bones), 4 (ARRAY and CHAOS) and 5 (ALL) count; 5 also takes the density out of this plugin's wakes, which are data-channel points. FluidNinja weights each tick's push of its river driver and brushes by the local density, so a tracked floater that paints density makes the current push harder along its path, even when its velocity is taken relative to the water. Set it on the NinjaLive in the level; changing it during play was not tested.

name: SplashSystem
comment: Defaults for bodies that set none of their own. The spray is spawned where a hull slams into the water or drives hard into it, scaled by how hard; any Niagara system works.

name: SplashReferenceWatts
comment: Splashes on one scale for every floating body and swimmer: a slam of this power (watts) makes a splash of strength 1 (the splash system at its own size), and the strength grows with the cube root of the power (eight times the power, twice the splash), so splash sizes compare across bodies, heights and stations. Each body's Splash Min Watts is its noise floor and its Splash Scale an art multiplier on top. At 70 W a 238 kg boat dropped 3 m (5.8 kW) throws a splash of 4.4, and a 175 kg crate dropped 3 m (35 kW) throws 8.

name: SplashStrengthCeiling
comment: The largest splash strength on the project's scale (a body's Max Splash Strength may cap its own lower).

name: SlapSound
comment: Hull sounds (none ship with the plugin; see the user guide, "Hull sounds"). Slap: a one-shot when a hull slams into the water. Wash: a looping sound of water running along the hull. Creak: a one-shot when the hull is thrown about. Their volume follows the water; a float input named "Pitch Shift" (semitones) is set on each, which MetaSounds can use.

name: bWaves
comment: FluidNinja Waves: floating bodies and the swimmer make real water waves in FluidNinja's own simulation (the modified NinjaLiveCore runs a wave field beside its fluid, on its pressure buffer's cells): each body's static head (how deep its hull sits below the wave-free surface) and the impulses of the slam and drag that stop it, written each frame into a source texture per simulation (User.WaveSourceTexture). FluidNinja's surface draws the waves (MF_NinjaOutput_BaseFunction_SURFACE) and the other floaters feel them: each body feels the waves of everything but itself (B - B_self, its own field taken out by a self field that follows it, and put back as radiation damping). Needs the modified NinjaLiveCore (User.WaveSimEnabled): a stock one makes no waves, with an error.

name: WaveDepthCm
comment: The water's depth the waves run at where FluidNinja's height field is off (User.Wave.DepthCm); where it is on, the core takes water Z minus its bed. The waves slow and steepen in shallow water (ω² = (g·k + σ/ρ·k³)·tanh(k·d)). Each simulation may override it, height field included (Wave Sims).

name: WaveDamping
comment: Damping of every wave (User.Wave.Damping, 1/s on the surface's vertical speed): 0.02 lets rings cross a pool.

name: WaveSpongeCm
comment: Width of the absorbing band at an open simulation window's edge (User.Wave.SpongeCm): waves running out of the window fade there instead of coming back in. Used only where Wave Edge Open is on. The bodies' own fields use the same width.

name: bWaveEdgeOpen
comment: The simulation window's border is open water (User.Wave.EdgeOpen 1: waves leave through the sponge), or a wall that reflects them (0, a walled pool). Each simulation may override it (Wave Sims).

name: WaveWallAbsorption
comment: Where a simulation's window border is a wall: how strongly it takes energy out of the waves reaching it (User.Wave.WallAbsorption, 1/s on the water's motion within Wave Wall Band of the wall), as a pool's gutter or skimmer does: a wall gives back most of a wave, not all of it. 0.4 returns about 80% of a 2 m wave's height. 0: the walls give back everything, and a closed basin keeps every wave (a floater's own waves then build up in it over minutes). The bodies' own fields use the same. Each simulation may override it.

name: WaveWallBandCm
comment: Width of the band along a walled window border that Wave Wall Absorption acts in (User.Wave.WallBandCm).

name: WaveShoreDepthCm
comment: Water shallower than this absorbs waves, more the shallower (a beach) (User.Wave.ShoreDepthCm).

name: WaveBreakingSlope
comment: Waves steeper than this slope (rise over run, cell to cell) break, and so do crests higher than 0.6 of the depth (User.Wave.BreakingSlope). 1.0: a safety net for the cell-sized spikes and columns a bad source makes (slopes of several), not a Stokes limit. At 0.4 it damped the near wake of any hull with vertical topsides (a row boat's convex hull steps from its draft to nothing at the waterline, and the linear wake of that step is steeper than 0.4 over much of the water around and behind it), and the towed row boat's Kelvin wake came out at 0.52 of the exact linear wake; at 1.0 it reads 1.00-1.03 (the bench's ripple-kelvin). Leaving the cells near a hull out of the judgement does not help: the steep water is the wake itself.

name: WaveHyperviscosity
comment: Damping of the shortest waves the grid carries (User.Wave.Hyperviscosity, 1/s at the grid's finest wavelength, falling as k⁴ for longer ones): keeps the cell-sized ripples a hull's sharp side makes from ringing.

name: WaveCurrentCoupling
comment: How much FluidNinja's current carries the waves (User.Wave.CurrentCoupling): 1 sweeps them down the creek with the water, 0 leaves them in still water.

name: WaveFeelScale
comment: κ: how much of the waves the floating bodies feel (times each body's own Wave Feel Scale). 1 is physical; 0 floats them on FluidNinja's own surface (the waves are still made and drawn).

name: bRadiationDamping
comment: The drag of each body's own waves, put back in every physics step (heave, roll and pitch, from its rest footprint at each motion's natural frequency), since what a body feels has its own waves taken out. Off: a body loses only what the other waves take from it, and bobs on for longer.

name: WaveAddedMassScale
comment: The water each body drags along as it heaves, rolls and pitches (its added mass, from its rest footprint on the simulation's cells by strip theory: ρ π B² / 8 per unit length of the footprint, times L / (L + B) for its ends; roll and pitch from the same strips by their arm squared), scaled by this. The body responds as the heavier system (a crate's heave period lengthens by about a third, a ball's by more) and its radiation damping is worked out at that slower frequency. 1 is physical; 0 none. Stable Steps carry it (the force is rewritten so the physics solver's own step lands where the heavier body's would): with Stable Steps off it does nothing.

name: bWaveDepthFromGround
comment: The bodies' own fields take the water's depth under each body from the ground below it (a trace down from the water), at most Wave Depth (or the simulation's override), as the core does with its landscape height field and Clamp Height Lower Values on: beds flattened by the clamp run at Wave Depth, only shallower ones at their own. Off: Wave Depth everywhere, as the core does with the height field off. Where the trace finds no ground, Wave Depth too. Off by default: a trace often meets a water mesh with collision at the surface and reads a depth of 1 cm.

name: bWaveDisplacement
comment: Source 1: each hull's static head, how deep it sits below the wave-free surface (open interiors included); its motion makes the impact rings, bow waves and the Kelvin wake.

name: bWaveImpulse
comment: Source 2: the slam and drag that stop a hull push the same impulse into the water, equal and opposite (the Cauchy–Poisson impulse problem).

name: WaveImpulseScale
comment: Scales the impulse source. The static head already radiates a falling body's waves; the slam and drag impulses add the part a linear field misses, and at 1 they counted the same water twice (impulse rings 2 to 3 times Evers' measurements). 0.35 matches the first crests of the ripple-evers bench.

name: WaveSourceSmoothCm
comment: The impulses are spread over a Gaussian this wide (σ), or three times the σ of the piece of hull each came from if that is wider, at most sixteen wave cells (under a quarter of a cell: bilinear between the four nearest cells). The impulse each puts in is unchanged.

name: MaxWaveImpulses
comment: The most impulse pieces (one per wet hull piece per physics step, all bodies) sent to the waves in a frame. Past it, each body's neighbouring pieces pressing the same way are merged into one at their centre (in squares of a wave cell, doubled until they fit), so the frame's whole impulse and where it lands are kept; this is logged once. 0 sends none.

name: bFoam
comment: The foam channel (needs a core at interface version 4): whitecaps where waves break, wake trails a moving hull's waterline sheds and impact rings where something lands, accumulated by the core per wave cell and drawn by the surface material; never fed back into the waves. Off: the core accumulates none and the surfaces stay clean; the waves are identical either way. fnb.Waves.Foam is the tiers' switch.

name: FoamDecay
comment: How fast the foam fades (User.Wave.FoamDecay, 1/s): 0.7 is an e-fold in about 1.4 s, a boat's trail gone in about 1.5 s.

name: FoamBreaking
comment: Scale of the foam breaking waves make (User.Wave.FoamBreaking): the breaking decay times the water's speed. The whitecaps.

name: FoamWake
comment: Scale of the foam a moving hull's waterline sheds (User.Wave.FoamWake): its static head's edge times its speed through the water. The wake trails and bow foam.

name: FoamImpact
comment: Scale of the foam an impulse makes (User.Wave.FoamImpact): slams, Add Water Impulse, pokes and swimmer strokes. The impact rings.

name: WaveHeightScaleParameter
comment: The surface material's scalar that scales the drawn wave height (MF_NinjaOutput_BaseFunction_SURFACE's WaveHeightScale): set to 0 on the captured surfaces' dynamic materials while the Surface Mirror is drawn, so the mirror shows FluidNinja's own surface W, and put back right after.

name: WaveNormalScaleParameter
comment: The surface material's scalar that scales how far the waves bend the drawn normal (MF_NinjaOutput_BaseFunction_SURFACE's WaveNormalScale): set on each simulation's surface dynamic materials (Wave Normal Scale Factor, or the simulation's override).

name: WaveNormalScaleFactor
comment: A simulation's surfaces get WaveNormalScale = this / (0.005 × its size in cm): 0.1 on a 20 m pool, 0.025 on an 80 m river, which keeps the drawn normal true to the waves' slope whatever the simulation's size.

name: PressureBufferParameter
comment: The surface material's texture parameter holding the simulation's pressure buffer (RT_PressureDivergence): on a wave simulation its B is the drawn wave height η + P and its A the static head P. Its size gives the wave cells (the simulation's size / its width). It is read only once the core has made it RGBA16F (a stock RG16F one has no B, and its A reads 1).

name: WaveSims
comment: Per simulation: overrides by NinjaLive actor name (its name or label), for a walled pool or a simulation of its own depth. Two ship for the demo level (FNB_DemoPool): Pool_FluidNinja, a closed pool 4 m deep, and River_FluidNinja, a river lane 3 m deep. A NinjaLive actor carrying a FluidNinja Wave Sim component (UFluidNinjaWaveSimComponent) is set up by that component instead, and an entry here naming it is ignored (logged once).

name: bSwimmerWaves
comment: Swimmers push the water aside (FluidNinja Waves' static head, as a hull's): the player's pawn by its capsule, upright, and each registered swimmer by its head, chest and hips, so swimming, wading and jumping in make waves. A pawn whose capsule has no collision (seated in a boat, a boarding clip) makes none. Needs Waves.

name: SwimmerVolumeLitres
comment: The swimmer's own volume, litres: the most water it pushes aside. Its capsule holds several times that (35 cm in radius and 180 cm tall: about 600 L, some 440 L of it under water while swimming), so the capsule's static head is scaled to take in at most this much. 76 L is a 75 kg swimmer at the human body's mean density, about 985 kg/m³ (75 / 985 m³).

name: bSwimmerContacts
comment: Swimmers' hands, forearms, feet and head (a diver's whole body) splash where they go into the water and press a ring into it (FluidNinja Waves), sized by how big they are and how fast they go in; feet kicking just under the surface churn it. The player's pawn (its skeletal mesh, while it is in the water) and every swimmer registered with UFluidNinjaBuoyancySubsystem::RegisterSwimmer (an AI swimmer or diver, say) take part. The splash is the project default (Effects → Splash System).

name: bPlayerContacts
comment: The player's pawn makes body-part splashes and rings too. Off: only registered swimmers do (turn it off if the pawn's own swim animation already spawns stroke splashes).

name: SwimmerEntryMinCmS
comment: A body part going in slower than this (straight down) makes no splash and no ring.

name: SwimmerSplashScale
comment: Scales the body parts' splashes (1: the splash a slam of the same power would make, Splash Reference Watts).

name: SwimmerImpulseScale
comment: Scales the body parts' impulses into the waves (1: the part's added mass times the speed it goes in at).

name: SwimmerCavitySeconds
comment: A part going in less than this long after another part of the same swimmer went in nearby (Swimmer Cavity Cm) enters the air pocket that one opened: a third of the splash and half the impulse. A pencil or head-first entry stays small (its body follows its feet or hands into their hole); a tuck, its hips and feet slapping in side by side at once, does not.

name: SwimmerCavityCm
comment: How near (across the surface) a part must go in to another's entry to enter its air pocket (Swimmer Cavity Seconds).

name: SwimmerKickDepthCm
comment: Feet moving up and down at most this deep under the surface churn it (a flutter kick), more the nearer they are.

name: SwimmerStrokeScale
comment: Scales the strokes' push on the water (FFluidNinjaSwimmerPose::StrokeImpulse, the FluidNinja Swimmer component's Add Stroke Impulse): the wake point a stroke writes into FluidNinja's point input and the small impulse it presses into the waves. 0: strokes do nothing.

name: bSwimmerWakes
comment: Swimmers write their push through the water into FluidNinja's point input as moving brush points (the Wake Data Channel, as the floating bodies' wakes), and a ring pushing outward where they plunge in. The player's pawn while its Character Movement swims over a water volume (wading: at each foot), and every registered swimmer in its water; either leaves the surface alone once its top is 50 cm under it. FluidNinja ignores points slower than about 40 cm/s, and a faster point paints dye that speeds a river up along its flow: at the default gain only the plunge ring and fast swimming against a current reach the water (Docs/FluidNinjaWaves.md, Wakes and the current). Needs no modified FluidNinja core. fnb.Buoyancy.Wake 0 turns these off with the floating bodies' wakes.

name: SwimmerWakeStrength
comment: The wake's target: the current plus this share of the swimmer's speed through the water (a hull's Wake Strength). Each frame the wake writes Swimmer Wake Gain of what the water at the swimmer still lacks of it.

name: SwimmerWakeGain
comment: Share of what the water at a swimmer still lacks of the target that the wake writes each frame (a hull's Wake Gain). FluidNinja ignores points under about 40 cm/s; above that it drives the water to about 2.3 times the written speed in still water and speeds a river up along its flow. Measured in the demo: at 0.2 a 3 m/s swimmer leaves no wake in still water, and swimming upstream speeds the river up around it by 1 to 1.3 m/s; at 0.6 still water shows a wake (about 0.5 m/s just behind the swimmer), but a river speeds up around a swimmer that only holds its place.

name: SwimmerWakeSizeCm
comment: Brush size of a swimmer's wake (it grows a little with speed). Wading uses two thirds of it at each foot, a plunge 1.2 times it.

name: SwimmerWakeMinSpeedCmS
comment: A swimmer moving slower than this through the water leaves no wake.

name: SwimmerCurrentRingInnerCm
comment: The current a swimmer is in is read on a ring around it, not under it, where its own wake is: from this far... The wakes read it there (they push only what the water around them lacks), and so does UFluidNinjaBuoyancySubsystem::GetCurrentAtLocation by default.

name: SwimmerCurrentRingOuterCm
comment: ...to this far (at least 10 cm past the inner radius).

name: bWaves
comment: This simulation makes waves. Off: it runs none (User.WaveSimEnabled false) and its floaters feel FluidNinja's own surface.

name: DepthCm
comment: This simulation's water depth for the waves everywhere in it (User.Wave.DepthCm), instead of the project's Wave Depth and of the depth FluidNinja's height field would give: the waves slow and steepen in shallow water. Read only while Depth From Bed is off.

name: bDepthFromBed
comment: The core takes the depth from FluidNinja's height field where it has one (water Z minus its bed, User.Wave.DepthFromBed), and the project's Wave Depth where it has none; Depth Cm is then not used. Off (the default): Depth Cm everywhere, for a pool or channel whose height field reads its water surface rather than its floor.

name: bWalled
comment: A closed basin: the simulation window's border is a wall that reflects the waves (User.Wave.EdgeOpen 0) and takes energy out of them within Wall Band of it at Wall Absorption, as a pool's gutter does. Off: open water, where waves leave through the sponge.

name: WallAbsorption
comment: How strongly a walled border takes energy out of the waves reaching it (User.Wave.WallAbsorption, 1/s on the water's motion within Wall Band of the wall): 0.4 returns about 80% of a 2 m wave's height; 0 returns everything, and a closed basin then keeps every wave a floater makes.

name: WallBandCm
comment: Width of the band along a walled border that Wall Absorption acts in (User.Wave.WallBandCm).

name: ScaleDownOverride
comment: The wave grid's scale-down for this simulation, 1, 2 or 4 (User.Wave.ScaleDown): its waves run on its pressure buffer's cells over this, so a tick costs a quarter at 2 and a sixteenth at 4, and the waves are drawn that much coarser. 0: the console variable fnb.Waves.ScaleDown, which the quality tiers (sg.WaterQuality) set.

name: Importance
comment: How much this simulation matters when fnb.Waves.MaxActiveSims keeps only the simulations nearest the camera running waves: its distance from the camera is divided by this before the simulations are ranked, so at 2 it counts as half as far away (the player's pool over a distant pond).

name: Description
comment: A line for the menu and the details panel: what this preset makes of an object.

name: Hull
comment: How the hull is built from the object's mesh.

name: HullResolutionCm
comment: From Collision: the hull surface's resolution (cm). Finer follows the shape better and costs more per step.

name: VoxelCount
comment: Voxels: how many cubes fill the collision.

name: SphereCount
comment: Sphere Row and Sphere Ring: how many spheres.

name: SphereRadiusScale
comment: The spheres' radius, as a multiple of the radius fitted to the object (One Sphere: the mean of its three half-extents; a row: the object's thinner half-extent; a ring: half the tube's thickness).

name: DensityKgM3
comment: Density: what the object is made of, kg/m³ (water 1000; pine 500, cork 240, ice 917, iron 7800; a beach ball about 8). Above 1000 it sinks.

name: RestDraftCm
comment: Rest Draft: how deep it floats at rest (cm).

name: Attitude
comment: Which way up it rests.

name: CentreOfMassShift
comment: Moves the centre of mass along the object's longest axis, as a share of its half-length (+0.3: a third of the way toward the axis' positive end). An arrow's steel head makes it float nose down; a bottle's base makes it stand up. 0 leaves it centred.

name: bSettleOnStart
comment: Put on the water at its rest draft and attitude when play starts, rather than dropped where it was placed.

name: bSleepWhenSettled
comment: Sleep once it has come to rest on still water, until something moves it or the water does.

name: bSetInteraction
comment: Also set how the body stirs FluidNinja (Interaction). Off, the component keeps its project's default: a preset made for one project should not hand bodies to FluidNinja's tracking in a project whose NinjaLives do not track.

name: Interaction
comment: The plugin's wakes, FluidNinja's own tracking (the modified core), or both.

name: bWake
comment: Write wake points where the hull moves through the water (a light prop carried by the current should not).

name: bWetLine
comment: Show the wet line on the hull (the hull material needs MF_FNB_HullWetness).

name: SplashMinWatts
comment: A slam weaker than this (watts) makes no splash: the body's noise floor.

name: MaxSplashStrength
comment: The largest splash this body throws, on the project's splash scale.

name: SplashScale
comment: An art multiplier on every splash of this body.
